mathematics.title: Mathematics
mathematics.define: A connected atlas of analysis, algebra, probability, foundations and geometry.
mathematics.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
mathematics.conventions: An arrow labeled prerequisite suggests study order. Contains and bridge arrows are navigation. Read each theorem's hypotheses before using it.

subject.complex-analysis.title: Complex analysis
subject.complex-analysis.define: Holomorphic rigidity, contour methods, analytic continuation and the geometry of Riemann surfaces.
subject.complex-analysis.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.complex-analysis.assumed_background: Real multivariable calculus, metric limits, elementary topology and line integration.
subject.complex-analysis.learning_outcomes:
- Use Cauchy theory to derive local analyticity and rigidity.
- Choose contour, residue and zero-counting arguments with the correct domain hypotheses.
- Separate local continuation from global single-valuedness.
subject.complex-analysis.study_route: [Holomorphic functions](./notes/ca.holomorphic.md) → [Cauchy–Goursat theorem](./notes/ca.cauchy.md) → [Cauchy integral formula](./notes/ca.cauchy-formula.md) → [Power series and analyticity](./notes/ca.series.md) → [Laurent series and isolated singularities](./notes/ca.singularities.md) → [Residue theorem](./notes/ca.residues.md) → [Montel's theorem](./notes/ca.normal.md) → [Riemann mapping theorem](./notes/ca.riemann-mapping.md)
subject.complex-analysis.graph_file: Open complex-analysis.json in the workspace graph list.
subject.complex-analysis.references:
- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.
- **CM** — John M. Lee. [Introduction to Complex Manifolds](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~lee/Books/ICM/). Author's book page.

subject.real-analysis.title: Real analysis
subject.real-analysis.define: Limits, measure, integration, convergence and the function spaces underlying modern analysis.
subject.real-analysis.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.real-analysis.assumed_background: Proof-based calculus, sequences, elementary linear algebra and set operations.
subject.real-analysis.learning_outcomes:
- Choose the correct convergence theorem before exchanging limits and integrals.
- Distinguish pointwise, almost-everywhere, uniform and norm convergence.
- Use measures, densities and weak derivatives as separate mathematical objects.
subject.real-analysis.study_route: [Completeness of the real numbers](./notes/ra.completeness.md) → [Metric limits and completeness](./notes/ra.metric.md) → [Measure spaces](./notes/ra.measure.md) → [Carathéodory extension](./notes/ra.outer.md) → [Lebesgue integration](./notes/ra.integral.md) → [Monotone convergence](./notes/ra.mct.md) → [Dominated convergence](./notes/ra.dct.md) → [Tonelli and Fubini](./notes/ra.fubini.md) → [Radon–Nikodym theorem](./notes/ra.rn.md) → [Lp spaces](./notes/ra.lp.md)
subject.real-analysis.graph_file: Open real-analysis.json in the workspace graph list.
subject.real-analysis.references:
- **RA** — Jeff Viaclovsky; notes by Ethan Brown. [MIT 18.125: Measure and Integration](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-125-measure-and-integration-fall-2003/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2003 lecture notes.
- **RA2** — Gerald B. Folland. [Real Analysis: Modern Techniques and Their Applications](https://www.wiley-vch.de/de/fachgebiete/mathematik-und-statistik/real-analysis-978-0-471-31716-6). Second edition, Wiley, 1999.

subject.functional-analysis.title: Functional analysis
subject.functional-analysis.define: Banach and Hilbert spaces, duality, operator theory and variational methods.
subject.functional-analysis.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.functional-analysis.assumed_background: Linear algebra, metric completeness, Lebesgue integration, Lp spaces and basic topology.
subject.functional-analysis.learning_outcomes:
- Track completeness and domain assumptions in the central Banach-space theorems.
- Distinguish weak, weak-star and norm topology.
- Choose the spectral theorem appropriate to the operator and formulate variational problems correctly.
subject.functional-analysis.study_route: [Banach spaces](./notes/fa.banach.md) → [Bounded linear operators](./notes/fa.operators.md) → [Continuous dual and bidual](./notes/fa.dual.md) → [Hahn–Banach extension theorem](./notes/fa.hahn-banach.md) → [Baire category theorem](./notes/fa.baire.md) → [Open mapping and bounded inverse](./notes/fa.open-mapping.md) → [Hilbert spaces and orthogonal projection](./notes/fa.hilbert.md) → [Compact self-adjoint spectral theorem](./notes/fa.compact-spectral.md)
subject.functional-analysis.graph_file: Open functional-analysis.json in the workspace graph list.
subject.functional-analysis.references:
- **FA** — Casey Rodriguez; Richard Melrose. [MIT 18.102: Introduction to Functional Analysis](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-102-introduction-to-functional-analysis-spring-2021/pages/lecture-notes-and-readings/). Spring 2021; includes Melrose's 2020 notes.
- **FA2** — Haim Brezis. [Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-70914-7). Springer, 2011.
- **FA3** — Gerald Teschl. [Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics](https://radon.mat.univie.ac.at/~gerald/ftp/book-schroe/index.html). Second edition, AMS, 2014; spectral theory.

subject.group-theory.title: Group theory
subject.group-theory.define: Symmetry through actions, quotient structures, finite-group structure and representation theory.
subject.group-theory.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.group-theory.assumed_background: Sets, maps, equivalence relations and finite-dimensional linear algebra; field basics for Galois theory.
subject.group-theory.learning_outcomes:
- Move between internal group structure, quotient maps and actions.
- Use Sylow arithmetic and conjugation to constrain finite groups.
- Relate representations and Galois groups to their underlying algebraic hypotheses.
subject.group-theory.study_route: [Groups and homomorphisms](./notes/gt.groups.md) → [Subgroups and generated subgroups](./notes/gt.subgroups.md) → [Cosets and Lagrange's theorem](./notes/gt.lagrange.md) → [Normal subgroups and quotients](./notes/gt.quotients.md) → [Group actions](./notes/gt.actions.md) → [Sylow theorems](./notes/gt.sylow.md) → [Derived series and solvable groups](./notes/gt.solvable.md) → [Linear representations](./notes/gt.representations.md) → [Characters and orthogonality](./notes/gt.characters.md)
subject.group-theory.graph_file: Open group-theory.json in the workspace graph list.
subject.group-theory.references:
- **GT** — J. S. Milne. [Group Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/GT.pdf). Version 4.01, 2025.
- **FT** — J. S. Milne. [Fields and Galois Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/FT.pdf). Version 5.10, 2022.

subject.number-theory.title: Number theory
subject.number-theory.define: Arithmetic from divisibility to number fields, local fields, prime distribution and rational points.
subject.number-theory.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.number-theory.assumed_background: Abstract algebra including rings and fields, elementary group theory, complex analysis for analytic topics.
subject.number-theory.learning_outcomes:
- Distinguish element factorization, prime-ideal factorization and class groups.
- Connect global arithmetic with completions and ramification.
- Separate proven distribution theorems from stronger error estimates and conjectures.
subject.number-theory.study_route: [Euclidean algorithm and unique factorization](./notes/nt.divisibility.md) → [Chinese remainder theorem](./notes/nt.crt.md) → [Finite fields](./notes/nt.finite-fields.md) → [Number fields, norm and trace](./notes/nt.number-fields.md) → [Algebraic integers](./notes/nt.integers.md) → [Dedekind domains and ideal factorization](./notes/nt.ideals.md) → [Ideal class group](./notes/nt.class-group.md) → [p-adic numbers and Hensel lifting](./notes/nt.padic.md) → [Riemann zeta function](./notes/nt.zeta.md)
subject.number-theory.graph_file: Open number-theory.json in the workspace graph list.
subject.number-theory.references:
- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.
- **NT2** — Andrew V. Sutherland. [MIT 18.785: Number Theory I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-785-number-theory-i-fall-2021/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2021 lecture notes.
- **NT3** — Keith Conrad. [The Local–Global Principle](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/localglobal.pdf). Author's expository notes; quadratic forms and failures of local-global principles.
- **FT** — J. S. Milne. [Fields and Galois Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/FT.pdf). Version 5.10, 2022.
- **EC** — J. S. Milne. [Elliptic Curves](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/EC2.pdf). Second edition, World Scientific, 2020; author-hosted text.

subject.probability-theory.title: Probability theory
subject.probability-theory.define: Measure-theoretic probability, limit laws, conditional expectation, martingales and stochastic processes.
subject.probability-theory.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.probability-theory.assumed_background: Measure and integration, Lp spaces, elementary real analysis and linear algebra.
subject.probability-theory.learning_outcomes:
- Identify the convergence mode and moment assumptions in each limit law.
- Formulate conditioning as an almost-everywhere integral identity.
- Check filtration, stopping-time and integrability conditions before stochastic calculations.
subject.probability-theory.study_route: [Probability spaces and random variables](./notes/pr.space.md) → [Independence and product laws](./notes/pr.independence.md) → [Modes of convergence](./notes/pr.convergence.md) → [Strong law of large numbers](./notes/pr.slln.md) → [Central limit theorem](./notes/pr.clt.md) → [Conditional expectation](./notes/pr.conditional.md) → [Filtrations and martingales](./notes/pr.martingale.md) → [Optional stopping](./notes/pr.stopping.md) → [Brownian motion](./notes/pr.brownian.md)
subject.probability-theory.graph_file: Open probability-theory.json in the workspace graph list.
subject.probability-theory.references:
- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.
- **PR2** — University of Cambridge, DPMMS. [Probability and Measure](https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/study/II/Probability%2BMeasure/2019-2020/lecture-notes-1-18.pdf). 2019–2020, lectures 1–18.

subject.set-theory-logic.title: Set theory and mathematical logic
subject.set-theory-logic.define: Syntax, semantics, computability and axiomatic set theory, with explicit metatheoretic assumptions.
subject.set-theory-logic.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.set-theory-logic.assumed_background: Proof techniques, elementary sets and functions; elementary arithmetic for coding computations.
subject.set-theory-logic.learning_outcomes:
- Distinguish provability, truth in a structure and logical validity.
- State incompleteness with effective-axiomatization and consistency assumptions.
- Distinguish internal cardinality, external cardinality and relative consistency.
subject.set-theory-logic.study_route: [Sets, functions and relations](./notes/sl.sets.md) → [First-order syntax and proofs](./notes/sl.syntax.md) → [Structures, satisfaction and elementary maps](./notes/sl.semantics.md) → [Gödel completeness theorem](./notes/sl.completeness.md) → [Compactness theorem](./notes/sl.compactness.md) → [Computability and enumerable theories](./notes/sl.computability.md) → [First incompleteness theorem](./notes/sl.incompleteness-one.md) → [Ordinals and well-orders](./notes/sl.ordinals.md) → [ZF axioms and the cumulative hierarchy](./notes/sl.zf.md) → [Continuum hypothesis and independence](./notes/sl.ch.md)
subject.set-theory-logic.graph_file: Open set-theory-logic.json in the workspace graph list.
subject.set-theory-logic.references:
- **LOGIC** — Open Logic Project contributors. [Open Logic Text](https://builds.openlogicproject.org/open-logic-complete.pdf). Living open textbook; first-order logic, computability and set theory.
- **MODEL** — David Marker. [Model Theory: An Introduction](https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~marker/mt-intro.html). Springer GTM 217, 2002.
- **SET** — Joel David Hamkins. [How the Continuum Hypothesis Could Have Been Fundamental](https://jdh.hamkins.org/wp-content/uploads/Slides-CH-could-have-been-fundamental-Hamkins-Oslo-June-2024.pdf). Oslo lecture slides, June 2024; independence background.
- **FORCING** — Joel David Hamkins. [Lectures on Set Theory](https://jdh.hamkins.org/lectures-on-set-theory-beijing-june-2025/). Peking University, June 2025; Lecture 3: Forcing.

subject.topology.title: Topology
subject.topology.define: Point-set foundations and algebraic topology, from compactness to homotopy, homology and duality.
subject.topology.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.topology.assumed_background: Sets, maps, equivalence relations, basic real analysis and groups for algebraic topology.
subject.topology.learning_outcomes:
- Keep compactness, separation and countability assumptions distinct.
- Compute homotopy and homology invariants by decomposition.
- Recognize the coefficient and orientation requirements in duality.
subject.topology.study_route: [Topological spaces and continuity](./notes/tp.spaces.md) → [Subspace, product and quotient topologies](./notes/tp.subspace.md) → [Compactness and Hausdorff spaces](./notes/tp.compact.md) → [Connectedness and path connectedness](./notes/tp.connected.md) → [Homotopies and homotopy equivalence](./notes/tp.homotopy.md) → [Fundamental group](./notes/tp.fundamental.md) → [Covering-space classification](./notes/tp.coverings.md) → [Singular homology](./notes/tp.homology.md) → [Cohomology and cup product](./notes/tp.cohomology.md)
subject.topology.graph_file: Open topology.json in the workspace graph list.
subject.topology.references:
- **TOP** — Allen Hatcher. [Notes on Introductory Point-Set Topology](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf). Author's course notes.
- **AT** — Allen Hatcher. [Algebraic Topology](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATpage.html). Cambridge University Press, 2002; author-hosted text.

subject.differential-geometry.title: Differential geometry
subject.differential-geometry.define: Smooth manifolds, differential forms, Riemannian geometry, curvature and global geometric theorems.
subject.differential-geometry.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.differential-geometry.assumed_background: Multivariable calculus, linear algebra, elementary ODEs and manifold topology.
subject.differential-geometry.learning_outcomes:
- Express differentiation and integration independently of a coordinate chart.
- Distinguish metric, connection and curvature data.
- Connect local differential geometry to global topological restrictions.
subject.differential-geometry.study_route: [Smooth manifolds and smooth maps](./notes/dg.smooth.md) → [Tangent spaces and differentials](./notes/dg.tangent.md) → [Differential forms and exterior derivative](./notes/dg.forms.md) → [Stokes' theorem](./notes/dg.stokes.md) → [de Rham theorem](./notes/dg.derham.md) → [Riemannian metrics](./notes/dg.metric.md) → [Levi-Civita connection](./notes/dg.levi-civita.md) → [Geodesics and the exponential map](./notes/dg.geodesics.md) → [Curvature and sectional curvature](./notes/dg.curvature.md)
subject.differential-geometry.graph_file: Open differential-geometry.json in the workspace graph list.
subject.differential-geometry.references:
- **DG** — John M. Lee. [Introduction to Smooth Manifolds](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~lee/Books/ISM/). Second edition, Springer, 2013; author's page.
- **RG** — John M. Lee. [Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~lee/Books/RM/). Second edition, Springer, 2018; author's page.
- **DG2** — Peter S. Park. [Hodge Theory](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~pspark/harvardminorthesis.pdf). Author's Harvard minor thesis exposition, Section 2.

subject.algebraic-geometry.title: Algebraic geometry
subject.algebraic-geometry.define: Commutative algebra, varieties and schemes, followed by local properties, divisors and cohomology of curves.
subject.algebraic-geometry.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.algebraic-geometry.assumed_background: Commutative algebra, modules and tensor products, elementary topology and field extensions.
subject.algebraic-geometry.learning_outcomes:
- Translate geometry into coordinate rings and local rings.
- Retain generic points and nilpotents when passing from varieties to schemes.
- Use divisors, line bundles and cohomology with smoothness and properness hypotheses.
subject.algebraic-geometry.study_route: [Commutative rings, ideals and modules](./notes/ag.rings.md) → [Noetherian rings and Hilbert basis theorem](./notes/ag.noetherian.md) → [Localization and local rings](./notes/ag.localization.md) → [Hilbert Nullstellensatz](./notes/ag.nullstellensatz.md) → [Prime spectrum and Zariski topology](./notes/ag.spec.md) → [Sheaves and stalks](./notes/ag.sheaves.md) → [Schemes and structure sheaves](./notes/ag.schemes.md) → [Scheme morphisms and fiber products](./notes/ag.morphisms.md) → [Smooth projective curves and genus](./notes/ag.curves.md) → [Riemann–Roch for curves](./notes/ag.riemann-roch.md)
subject.algebraic-geometry.graph_file: Open algebraic-geometry.json in the workspace graph list.
subject.algebraic-geometry.references:
- **AG** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Geometry](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AG.pdf). Version 6.10, 2024.
- **CAALG** — J. S. Milne. [A Primer of Commutative Algebra](https://www.jmilne.org/math/xnotes/ca.html). Author's course notes.
- **STACKS** — The Stacks Project Authors. [The Stacks Project](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/browse). Living reference; schemes, morphisms and algebraic curves.
